cards.text: This is the word of the LORD that came to Hosea (Hosea 1:1), and here it's about His people, Israel. The LORD starts way back, when Israel was a child, and He says He loved him. Friend, this is a dad pulling out the OLD baby pictures.

cards.question: When Israel was a child, the LORD loved him and called His son out of ___.

cards.text: So the LORD keeps calling Israel, over and over. Let's see how that goes.

cards.question: The more the LORD called Israel, the closer they came to Him.
While Israel kept walking away from the LORD, who were they sacrificing to?

cards.text: Now the LORD gets tender: He calls Israel Ephraim here too, and He says He taught Ephraim to walk, holding them by the arms. I've watched toddlers walk, friend, and it's mostly falling forward with confidence.

cards.question: Ephraim realized it was the LORD who healed them.
The LORD taught Ephraim to walk. How does He say He led them?

cards.text: Cords of kindness, ropes of love. Then He lifted the yoke off their necks, like that heavy bag strap finally sliding off your shoulder at the end of a LONG day.

cards.question: After lifting the yoke from their necks, the LORD bent down to ___ them.

cards.text: Then the message turns, and the LORD asks: won't they go back to Egypt and be ruled by the nation of Assyria? Egypt, friend, the place He called them OUT of.

cards.question: Why does the LORD say Israel is headed back to Egypt and under Assyria?

cards.text: A sword will flash through their cities and destroy the bars of their gates. It will consume them in their own plans.
And the LORD says His people are bent on turning from Him. Not wandering off by accident, BENT on it.

cards.question: Even though Israel calls to the Most High, He will by no means lift them up.

cards.text: After all those warnings, the LORD speaks to Ephraim again. This time, He asks a question.

cards.question: Right after all those warnings, what does the LORD ask Ephraim?

answers.text: How could I give you up

cards.text: He keeps asking how He could make them like Admah or treat them like Zeboiim. Those are towns the LORD overthrew along with Sodom and Gomorrah (Deuteronomy 29:23).

cards.question: The LORD says His heart is turned within Him and His ___ is stirred.
The LORD says He will execute the full fury of His anger on Ephraim.
Why does the LORD say He won't destroy Ephraim again?

answers.text: He is God and not man
The prophet begged Him to stop

cards.question: The LORD, the Holy One among His people, says He will come in wrath.

cards.text: Then the LORD looks ahead. He's going to make a sound nobody could sleep through, not even the dead batteries I shared that drawer with.

cards.question: Looking ahead, the LORD says He will roar like a ___.
When the LORD roars, His children run away from Him.

cards.text: They come trembling like birds from Egypt and like doves from the land of Assyria. DOVES, friend, and my Minty would be passing notes down the whole counter about this one.

cards.question: After His children come trembling back, where does the LORD settle them?

answers.text: In a city by the sea

cards.text: And the LORD signs it Himself: declares the LORD. I know what it's like to get called out of a dark place, friend, so hearing Him promise to settle His children in their homes gets me every single time.

findings.problem: Hosea is named in the opening card, but the card never says simply who he is, such as identifying him as a prophet.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The blank asks for Egypt, but the opening story card only says that the LORD loved Israel as a child. Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason out the place; this is completing wording the baker has not seen.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The second sentence retells Hosea 11:1 by saying Egypt is the place the LORD called Israel out of, but the card's citation covers only Hosea 11:5.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The stop moves straight to the LORD's roar and never tells verse 10's opening statement that they will walk after the LORD. That omits the important reversal from turning away from Him to following Him.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The setup only says that the LORD will make a loud sound, which does not distinguish a lion from a bear. The blank asks the baker to guess an unseen word in the simile rather than reason out what the picture means.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This is a where question, but "In a city by the sea" is a generic invented location rather than a real detail from somewhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.
